Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with `README.md` and the required wake-visual-signals skill. That skill applies directly here: it requires inspecting multi-wake flow keyframes before I change the dogfish target policy. After that I’ll trace the assigned parent, sampled results, inherited logs, and current rollout evidence, then produce one candidate and update both required evidence files.

The rendered contract identifies `solver_4466c38d0079` as the policy parent and `optimizer_ed2348772c01` as the assigned guidance parent. All four sampled scores shown in the contract are identical successful rollouts, so I’ll verify whether their policy files and detailed evidence are also identical before choosing a supported change.

The policy hashes differ, but the released keyframe sheet and every physical/scoring field (except wall time) are identical across the four current samples. That makes them one deterministic `20.25°`/scale-`0.30` result, not four trials. I’m now applying the skill’s visual pass to the common prewarm and the released rollout, then I’ll compare it with the closest inherited negative one-axis result because no current sampled rollout is a termination failure.

The latest inherited one-axis tests sharpen the decision. Closing-speed-based steering relief (`0.30→0.32` while closing) delayed capture to `256.66` and worsened mean distance to `7.394L`; increasing bearing-rate lead alone (`0.25→0.30`) was worse still at `270.45` and `8.499L`, with an extra large upper reversal visible before wake entry. I’m cross-checking their detailed diagnostics now; the candidate direction will preserve propulsion and test the opposite, bounded rate-lead direction rather than combine axes.

The diagnostic cross-check supports an isolated symmetric test: the `0.30` lead rollout had identical anterior gait maxima but changed mean relative x-flow from `+0.00793` to `-0.00055`, added an upper reversal, delayed capture by `25.90`, and raised RMS lateral force. I’ll first record that visual diagnosis and the `0.25→0.20` hypothesis in the required notes, as the skill mandates; only then will I edit the policy.

The candidate and durable guidance are both updated. The guidance now corrects the stale “four `20°` samples” statement to the actual duplicated `20.25°` result and records the two evaluated steering regressions with explicit avoid/falsification boundaries. I’m moving to the mandated checker now; this does not run CFD.
